evidence.claim: Volcanic basins and wooded heights frame a drive to mining country.
evidence.quote: The gravel road winds through volcanic caldera now overgrown with pinyons and junipers along the skirts of the range. Towards the peaks of the range, aspens and ponderosa pines grow profusely.

evidence.claim: Volcanic basins and wooded heights frame a drive to mining country.
evidence.quote: Stop at the historical Pioche mining town as you work your way through the Wilson Range

evidence.claim: Mount Wilson Back Country Byway crosses broad basins and narrow canyons on gravel, dirt and paved roads.
evidence.quote: The route follows gravel, dirt, and paved roads through volcanic basins, narrow canyons, pinyon-juniper woodlands, and higher-elevation stands of aspen and ponderosa pine.

evidence.claim: Pinyons and junipers grow across volcanic terrain, with aspen and ponderosa pine higher in the range.
evidence.quote: The gravel road winds through volcanic caldera now overgrown with pinyons and junipers along the skirts of the range. Towards the peaks of the range, aspens and ponderosa pines grow profusely.

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Land Management identifies it as a Type II Back Country Byway and highlights its landscape, historic cabins and pioneer cemetery.
evidence.quote: Mt. Wilson Back Country Byway - Type II

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Land Management identifies it as a Type II Back Country Byway and highlights its landscape, historic cabins and pioneer cemetery.
evidence.quote: Explore historical cabins or visit a pioneer cemetery.

evidence.claim: Recreation.gov allows two to four hours for the drive.
evidence.quote: Allow 2 to 4 hours.

evidence.claim: The corridor reaches Pioche, where a silver mine opened in 1864.
evidence.quote: The first modern settlement of the area occurred in 1864 with the opening of a silver mine.

evidence.claim: By the early 1870s, the town had become one of Nevada's important silver-mining centers.
evidence.quote: By the early 1870s, Pioche had grown larger to become one of the most important silver-mining towns in Nevada.

evidence.claim: A later change came to nearby Spring Valley: a dam built in 1965 stored water for agriculture, and the reservoir area became a state park in 1969.
evidence.quote: The Eagle Valley Dam was built on Meadow Valley Wash in 1965, creating the Eagle Valley Reservoir for agricultural usage. The area around the reservoir was designated a state park in 1969.

evidence.claim: On the approach to Pioche, Spring Valley State Park lies at the east end of State Route 322, near Ursine.
evidence.quote: The state park is located at the east end of Nevada State Route 322, 20 miles (32 km) east of the town of Pioche and near the village of Ursine.

evidence.claim: Ursine sits downstream from Eagle Valley Reservoir in the foothills of the White Rock Mountains.
evidence.quote: It is located in the foothills of the White Rock Mountains on Eagle Valley about two miles downstream from the Eagle Valley Reservoir in Spring Valley State Park.

evidence.claim: Continue toward Pioche, where abandoned tramway cables and ore buckets remain over parts of town.
evidence.quote: The abandoned tramway used cables which still stretch over parts of the town, with some original ore buckets intact.

evidence.claim: Eagle Valley Reservoir began as an agricultural water project.
evidence.quote: creating the Eagle Valley Reservoir for agricultural usage.

evidence.claim: The Eagle Valley Dam was built across Meadow Valley Wash in 1965, and the land surrounding the reservoir received state-park designation four years later.
evidence.quote: The Eagle Valley Dam was built on Meadow Valley Wash in 1965, creating the Eagle Valley Reservoir for agricultural usage. The area around the reservoir was designated a state park in 1969.

evidence.claim: The park adjoins the 65-acre reservoir and includes historic ranch buildings.
evidence.quote: Spring Valley State Park is a public recreation area adjoining the 65-acre (26 ha) Eagle Valley Reservoir

evidence.claim: The park adjoins the 65-acre reservoir and includes historic ranch buildings.
evidence.quote: The park offers camping, fishing, a boat launch, picnicking, hiking trails, historic ranch buildings, and a group-use area.

evidence.claim: It lies near Ursine at the east end of State Route 322, 20 miles east of Pioche.
evidence.quote: The state park is located at the east end of Nevada State Route 322, 20 miles (32 km) east of the town of Pioche and near the village of Ursine.

evidence.claim: The reservoir area combines hiking trails with a boat launch and places to picnic, beside the historic ranch buildings.
evidence.quote: The park offers camping, fishing, a boat launch, picnicking, hiking trails, historic ranch buildings, and a group-use area.

evidence.claim: High-clearance vehicles are recommended for the byway. The route is generally seasonal and can become unsafe or impassable in winter or when wet.
evidence.quote: High-clearance vehicles are recommended. Allow 2 to 4 hours. The route is generally open seasonally and may become unsafe or impassable in winter, after heavy rain, or when roads are wet.

evidence.claim: Ursine lies in Eagle Valley below the White Rock Mountains, about two miles downstream from Eagle Valley Reservoir.
evidence.quote: It is located in the foothills of the White Rock Mountains on Eagle Valley about two miles downstream from the Eagle Valley Reservoir in Spring Valley State Park.

evidence.claim: Its post office opened in 1895 and operated until 1959.
evidence.quote: A post office was established at Ursine in 1895, and remained in operation until 1959.

evidence.claim: Ore once traveled above Pioche in buckets suspended from an aerial tramway.
evidence.quote: An aerial tramway carried buckets of ore from the mines to the Godbe Mill.

evidence.claim: During the 1920s and 1930s, the system carried silver and nickel ore from the mines to the Godbe Mill; cables and some original buckets remain over parts of town.
evidence.quote: The tramway ran during the 1920s and 1930s and was used for the transportation of silver and nickel ore. The abandoned tramway used cables which still stretch over parts of the town, with some original ore buckets intact.

evidence.claim: Silver mining had begun here in 1864, and by the early 1870s Pioche ranked among Nevada's important silver-mining towns.
evidence.quote: By the early 1870s, Pioche had grown larger to become one of the most important silver-mining towns in Nevada.

evidence.claim: Silver mining had begun here in 1864, and by the early 1870s Pioche ranked among Nevada's important silver-mining towns.
evidence.quote: The first modern settlement of the area occurred in 1864 with the opening of a silver mine.

evidence.claim: Two theaters overlook downtown: Thompson's Opera House, built in 1873, and the Gem Theater, built in 1937.
evidence.quote: Two historic theaters site side by side on a hill overlooking downtown. Thompson's Opera House was built in 1873 and restored in 2009 while the Gem Theater was built in 1937

evidence.claim: The opera house was restored in 2009, while restoration of the neighboring cinema began in 2022.
evidence.quote: Thompson's Opera House was built in 1873 and restored in 2009 while the Gem Theater was built in 1937 and ongoing restoration began in 2022.
